STUDY HALL COURSES:
Reporting On Politics 101
Reporting on local and national politics can feel opaque to those who have yet to crack the code. Perhaps more than even culture writing, politics requires knowledge of a specific, technical kind of language. In this
class
, Grace Byron will guide you on how to generate ideas, find outlets, and use the lingo that veteran politics reporters and editors use when building a story. From interviewing subjects, write-arounds, and opinion pieces, you will analyze a few pitches and stories to get a better sense of how to get started. You'll leave this one-hour class feeling prepared to start your political reporting journey and hopefully have a few ideas of how to get tips and pitch new editors.
Grace’s work has appeared in
The New Yorker,
Vogue
, and
The Nation
.
The 1.5 hour course will take place August 17th 10 AM PDT.
The standard price is $99. Study Hall members can use the discount code “
studyhallmember
” to bring the price to $49.50. For any questions, email
support@studyhall.xyz
.
Sign up
.
A Beginner’s Guide to Covering the Sex Industry
Sex work seems to be everywhere these days. Storylines about sex workers have popped up in shows like
Euphoria
,
Margo’s Got Money Troubles
, and
Hacks
. Yet even as OnlyFans has become a household name, few journalists actually understand the inner workings of this often underground industry — or how to build trust that’s needed to get sex worker sources to open up about these stories.
In this
course
, Lux Alptraum, an adult industry expert and one-time editor of the porn blog Fleshbot, will walk you through the basics of reporting on the sex industry. In addition to providing an overview of the different corners of the sex industry, she’ll also explain why so many sex workers do not trust journalists, and walk participants through the best practices for covering adult industry-related topics.
The 1.5 hour course will now take place September 18th at 10 AM PDT/ 1 PM ET.
The standard price is $99. Study Hall members can use the discount code “studyhallmember” to bring the price to $49.50. For any questions, email
support@studyhall.xyz
.
Sign up
.
Interview With Tyler Donohue
On the latest
episode
of the Study Hall Podcast, Tyler Donohue — a writer whose work has appeared in
The Cut
,
The Guardian
, and
Business Insider
— discussed writing about non-monogamy, cults, and intimacy.
The episode is available on
Apple Podcasts
.
Writing About Cults, Intimacy, and Non-monogamy ft. Tyler Donohue
Podcast Episode · The Study Hall Podcast · August 10 · 32m
Apple Podcasts
ICYMI: Interview With Andrew Durbin
On this podcast
episode
, Andrew Durbin, the editor in chief of
Frieze
, discussed how he researched the artists Peter Hujar and Paul Thek for his book
The Wonderful World That Almost Was
.
ICYMI:
Gaby Del Valle on covering far-right conservatism.
Brock Colyar on scene reporting.
Suzy Exposito on the future of Latino media.
Emily Gould on essays, envy, and exposure.
Call For Podcast Guests
We’re currently looking for new guests for the podcast! We’d love to spotlight longform reporting from the Study Hall community. If you have published a piece of longform reporting in 2026 and would like to be a guest on the podcast, please reach to
daniel@studyhall.xyz
. Check out our previous episodes spotlighting longform journalism by
Adam Popescu
,
Marianne Dhenin
, and
Allegra Rosenberg
.
Recommended Reading:
“What Makes An Adaptation Good?”, Richard Brody,
The New Yorker
“Revisiting the Ethics Code,” Liz Skalka,
Columbia Journalism Review
Comings and Goings:
Andrew Ackerman is
leaving
The Washington Post
. He’ll be joining
Bloomberg
to cover the Fed.
Danyel Smith is
joining
The Atlantic
as a staff writer.
Thom Bettridge is
stepping down
as editor in chief of
I-D
.
Emily Feng is
joining
NPR as a White House correspondent.
Plug Your Work
Please
submit
your work via our members site to share your work across our newsletters, blog, and social media channels.
Julia Rittenberg Profiled Romance Novelists
For
Playgirl
, Jill Rittenberg interviewed romance novelists about their work. Rittenberg told Study Hall: "I dug into the craft of writing sex and why it matters to storytelling. Authors Alicia Thompson, Lana Ferguson, Allie Oleander, and Isabelle Popp gave me their thoughts on the craft."
Nana Asfour Wrote About Her Childhood In Lebanon
For
McSweeney's
, Nana Asfour reflected on growing up during Lebanon's brutal civil war. Asfour told
Study Hall
: "In a hybrid first-person narrative and reporting essay for McSweeney’s new non-fiction section, I wrote about war, childhood friendships, shelters and giant tweezers."
Topacio "Topaz" Servellon Wrote About The Impact of Expanding The DeConcini Border Crossing
For
Tucson Spotlight
, Topacio "Topaz" Servellon reported on how "a federal proposal to expand the DeConcini border crossing would demolish a historic Nogales neighborhood." Servellon told
Study Hall
:"No one really talks about the mental health toll that comes with covering the border and immigration. I fell into a deep depression for two weeks. Then I dragged myself to a public meeting about a border port expansion, a city over. I wrote the story anyway. And when I finished it? I was proud. Really proud, actually! Turns out I can still do my job, even after a funk. Reminder for all journalists out there: Taking time away doesn't make you any less of a journalist."
Karli Poliziani Wrote A Travel Guide To Saint-Tropez
For
Condé Nast Traveler
, Karli Poliziani wrote about "the best places to eat, stay, and drink rosé in Saint-Tropez for Summer 2026, before the debut of the highly anticipated
The White Lotus
season 4—set to make Saint-Tropez an even buzzier hotspot for the Euro summer crowd."
